### 2.2 The room-count bridge — the gap Rev 1 did not examine

The plan needs +840,000 bed-nights while simultaneously constraining supply. That is not obviously possible, and the review was right to press it. Illustrative reconciliation:

| Source of bed-nights | Beds | Occupancy assumption | Bed-nights | Note |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Baseline licensed stock, Y0 utilisation | 11,000 | 32% | 1.28m | Current |
| **Same stock, deseasonalised** | 11,000 | 42% | **1.69m** | +410k with **zero new beds** — the cheapest 49% of the requirement |
| Registration of existing unregistered STL stock | +2,600 | 30% | **+285k** | Brings existing beds into the licensed, taxed, standards-bound system; not new construction |
| Conversion of vacant/heritage building stock | +900 | 40% | **+131k** | Priority instrument: reuse, no new footprint, heritage funding synergy |
| New-build, headroom-gated only | +250 | 45% | **+41k** | Small, and only where wastewater and water headroom is already proven |
| **Total** | 14,750 | — | **2.15m** | Against 2.12m required |

Two conclusions the bridge forces. **Deseasonalisation and registration deliver 83% of the requirement without a single new building** — which reframes the whole supply argument, and makes the constraint-vs-growth contradiction largely apparent rather than real. And new-build is a residual of ~250 beds over five years, which is politically defensible in a way that a growth target without a bridge never is.

## 3. Which visitors — source markets and segments

"International visitors" is not a market. Attracting the wrong ones is worse than attracting fewer.

Weights agreed with the finance and air-access teams before scoring (illustrative; working sheet available). Note the new criterion — **inbound travel emissions per visitor-night** — which the review rightly identified as the largest unexamined exposure.

| Criterion | Weight | DE/AT/CH | Nordics | UK/IE | US NE/West | Japan/Korea | Gulf | **Domestic + diaspora** |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Spend per trip (observed behaviour) | 18% | 4 | 4 | 3 | 5 | 4 | 5 | 2 |
| Length of stay | 12% | 5 | 5 | 3 | 4 | 3 | 3 | 3 |
| Willingness to travel off-peak | 15% | 4 | 4 | 3 | 3 | 2 | 2 | **5** |
| Interest in nature/heritage over resort product | 12% | 5 | 5 | 3 | 4 | 4 | 2 | 4 |
| Access without new route subsidy | 12% | 4 | 3 | 5 | 2 | 2 | 3 | **5** |
| **Inbound emissions per visitor-night (low = high score)** | 12% | **5** | 4 | 4 | **1** | **1** | 2 | **5** |
| Cost of acquisition | 9% | 4 | 4 | 4 | 2 | 3 | 3 | **5** |
| Low-impact on-site behaviour (guided, rule-following) | 10% | 4 | 4 | 3 | 3 | 5 | 3 | 3 |
| **Weighted total** | | **4.32** | **4.13** | **3.51** | **3.09** | **2.94** | **2.96** | **3.94** |

**Recommendation:** **German-speaking Europe and the Nordics as the beachhead** (rail- and short-haul-reachable, off-peak-willing, heritage-affine); **domestic and diaspora as the year-round base and seasonal filler**, promoted to a core market rather than an afterthought; **UK/Ireland as volume ballast on existing capacity**; **US long-haul deferred to Year 3 and capped**; **Japan/Korea kept warm as market five.**

Runners-up, one line each — and note the deliberate change from Rev 1:

- **US long-haul** — highest spend per trip, but a transatlantic return is roughly 1.7–2.3 t CO₂e per visitor, which at 5 nights is an order of magnitude above anything happening in-destination. Retained but **capped at ≤12% of arrivals**, entered only with 7+ night itineraries, and reported inside the full-footprint metric (§10). This is the honest reason for caution, and it is stronger than the route-economics reason given in Rev 1.
- **Japan/Korea** — excellent on-site behaviour and heritage affinity; same emissions objection, plus Japanese- and Korean-language service depth we do not have. Sequence, not exclusion.
- **Gulf** — high spend, poor seasonality fit, and a **product mismatch** with a walking-and-heritage proposition. *(Rev 1 said "assortment mismatch." That was retail vocabulary carried over unedited; the reviewer was right to notice and it is corrected.)*

**Domestic and diaspora — promoted from footnote to pillar.** Rev 1 treated residents and domestic visitors as a 20% quota reservation, which the review correctly called a partial answer. They are in fact: the off-season filler that makes lever C possible; the political constituency that legitimises quotas; and the resilience base when international demand shocks, as it did in 2009 and 2020. Actions: domestic shoulder-season campaign from month 4 (earlier than any international activity, because it needs no capacity governance); diaspora "roots and heritage" programme with the craft and archive product in §4; resident free-access card at all Showcase sites; school and youth programme funded from the levy.

**Segments to pursue, in order:** independent slow travellers (35–65, 5+ nights); specialist small-group operators (8–14 pax, guided, shoulder); heritage and craft special-interest; scientific, academic and volunteer field programmes; small-scale creative residencies and off-season MICE.

**Segments to decline, and to say so out loud:** cruise day-calls beyond a hard cap; large coach circuits using the region as a two-hour photo stop; any model dependent on free access to a site we are spending money to protect. *This remains a genuinely unsettled view: two board colleagues consider a cruise cap to be money left on the table, and their position deserves the real argument rather than the flattering one. §5.1 now provides it, including the part that cuts against me.*

---

## 4. Positioning — lead with the place, let the ethics be discovered

Sustainability should be verifiable, documented and impossible to miss for anyone who looks. It should almost never be the headline. Visitors book a place because it moves them; they *forgive* a place its rules because it moved them first. Campaigns that lead with virtue attract audiences who came to approve rather than to spend.

- **Not:** "Visit the region sustainably."
- **Proposed:** depth — few places, entered slowly, with someone who belongs there.
- **Working line, external:** **"Go slowly. You will be shown more."**
- *Rev 1 proposed "Not everything here is open. That is the point." It is a better sentence and a worse strategy. Combined with levies, fees and quotas it hands the "tourism for the rich, closed to our own people" attack to whoever wants it, and that attack has ended this strategy in other regions. Retained for internal use only, and paired with §4.2.*

### 4.1 Competitive set — named, with the wedge stated

The review noted, fairly, that this section was missing. Illustrative pending Stage 0 research; the discipline matters more than the current values.

| Comparator | Proposition | Typical stay / spend-day | Their advantage | **Our wedge** |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Slovenia (Julian Alps / Soča)** | Green-certified nature, close-in | 4.5 nts / €110 | Certification lead, rail access, price | Living heritage depth and craft; they are thinner on cultural continuity |
| **Northern Portugal / Douro** | Landscape + food + heritage | 4.0 nts / €125 | Wine brand, air access, weather | Genuine off-season product; Douro is peak-concentrated |
| **Scottish Highlands / Islands** | Wild landscape, distillery culture | 5.0 nts / €140 | Global brand recognition | Cost, and visible congestion management they are struggling with |
| **Norwegian fjords** | Iconic landscape at premium | 4.0 nts / €190 | Unmatched scenery | Price accessibility; and we are not cruise-dominated |
| **Transylvania / Maramureș** | Authentic rural heritage, low cost | 4.0 nts / €70 | Price, authenticity narrative | Service reliability, interpretation quality, walkable linked routes |
| **South Tyrol** | Managed alpine quality benchmark | 5.5 nts / €165 | Best-in-class execution | Not a comparator to beat — the model to study |

**Honest reading:** we are not the cheapest, the most iconic, or the best known. The defensible intersection is **linked multi-day routes + continuing living craft and food practice + genuine off-season openness + interpretation authored by people who belong there**. That intersection is contested but not held. €125/day sits credibly between Transylvania and Douro; 4.6 nights requires the linked-route product in §4.3 actually existing, which is why Phase B funds waymarking before it funds advertising.

### 4.2 Resident and domestic access equity — the pre-emptive political answer

Scarcity instruments fail politically unless residents are visibly the beneficiaries. To be adopted as binding, not aspirational:

- **Resident access card:** free entry, all Showcase sites, all year, no booking requirement outside peak instantaneous limits.
- **Quota reservation:** 25% of all timed slots held for residents and domestic visitors, released to general sale at 24 hours.
- **Levy transparency:** every resident household receives a one-page annual statement of levy income and what it built locally. The levy is defensible only for as long as it is legible.
- **Access days:** each Showcase site closed to commercial groups on defined community days.
- **Narrative discipline:** the message is *"the rules exist so that this stays yours,"* never *"the rules exist because visitors are a problem."* Both are true; only one holds a coalition together.

### 4.3 Product architecture

| Tier | Content | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| **Showcase** | 3–4 hero sites, timed entry, hard daily *and instantaneous* caps, custodian-authored interpretation | Reason to travel |
| **Dispersal network** | 12–18 secondary villages, valleys, trails, monuments on a linked multi-day route | Spreads load, spreads money, extends stay |
| **Depth experiences** | Craft workshops, harvest and food seasons, transhumance, restoration work, archives | Justifies price and extra nights |
| **Off-season proposition** | Weather-honest winter and shoulder product: storms, festivals, dark skies, quiet interiors, indoor craft | Lever C — highest leverage in the document |

**Exemplars, cited with their caveats** *(Rev 1 cited these too flatteringly; corrected):*
- **Bhutan** — high-value/low-volume via the Sustainable Development Fee, but the SDF was **halved from $200 to $100 in 2023** when arrivals failed to recover. The lesson is that price-based scarcity has an elasticity limit and must be calibrated, not merely asserted.
- **Palau** — the pledge is symbolic and excellent communications; the money instrument is the **Pristine Paradise Environmental Fee**. Do not confuse the two.
- **Faroe Islands** — "Closed for Maintenance" generated real earned media, on a very small base. It does not scale linearly and should be treated as a one-time reputational asset, not a channel.
- **South Tyrol** — the least glamorous and most useful model: bed-cap planning, quality-based licensing, year-round employment.

Off-season marketing is not a communications task. It works only if operators, transport and staffing stay open — which means the operating guarantee and the **labour retention** instrument (§6.5) must be committed *before* the campaign, not after it.

---

## 5. Protecting the asset — instruments, with authority stated

| Instrument | Design | **Who holds the lever** | Indicative effect (real) |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Timed-entry quotas** | Bookable slots; daily *and* instantaneous caps from Stage 0 study; 25% resident/domestic reservation; 15% released 48h out | Region (site management) | Removes peak crush without reducing receipts |
| **Visitor levy** | €3.00/bed-night, all paid accommodation incl. registered STL | **National enabling legislation required** — not yet in force; critical path item | 2.12m × €3 = **€6.4m/yr** at Y5; €3.9m at Y2 |
| **Site access fee** | €8–15 Showcase sites; residents free | Region | €2.5–4.0m/yr |
| **Cruise call cap + per-pax charge** | Max 1 vessel/day, seasonal window, €12/pax | **National port authority; existing call contracts run 2–4 yrs ahead** — negotiation, not decision | See §5.1 |
| **Vehicle management** | Park-and-ride to hero sites, coach permits by slot, no new mountain parking | Region + municipalities | Protects the experience, which protects the price |
| **Infrastructure-headroom licensing rule** | No accommodation licence where wastewater, water or waste headroom is not already proven | Region (planning) | The unglamorous clause that prevents the failure mode most destinations actually suffer |
| **STL registration + neighbourhood caps** | Mandatory registration; per-neighbourhood ceilings | Region, subject to §8 legal test | Brings 2,600 beds into the system (§2.2) |
